name: Abu Dhabi
summary: Abu Dhabi Global Market licenses captive insurers under the Captive Insurance Business Rulebook of the Financial Services Regulatory Authority. The current text is CIB VER07.270426, effective 27 April 2026. The first version, CIB VER01.041015, took effect on 21 October 2015. ADGM was established as a financial free zone under Federal Decree No. 15 of 2013. Rule 1.3.3 states that an insurer that is not incorporated in ADGM cannot be a captive insurer. The Rules authorise four classes. A Class 1 captive insures only risks of the group to which it belongs. A Class 2 captive may obtain no more than 20 percent of gross written premium from third-party risks arising from business or operations closely linked to that group. A Class 3 captive insures only persons engaged in similar, related, or common business, activities, trade, services, or operations, and it is owned by those persons or by a body corporate of which all of them are members. A Class 4 captive is an entity that the Regulator decides does not meet Class 1, 2, or 3. A cell company may carry on the business through class captive cells. Minimum capital is the highest of a base amount, a premium-risk component, and a technical-provision component, and the Regulator may direct a higher amount. The base is $150,000 for Class 1, $250,000 for Class 2, $500,000 for Class 3, and $1 million for Class 4. The Regulator may set a different base for Class 2, Class 3, and Class 4. The premium-risk component is 18 percent of net written premium up to $5 million and 16 percent above that. The technical-provision component is 5 percent of the net claims reserve for general business and 2.5 percent of actuarial policyholder liabilities for long-term business. A cell company holds at least $50,000 of non-cellular eligible capital. An active cell maintains the higher of net cellular assets of at least $50,000 and a risk-based test using the same premium and technical-provision percentages. The Fees Rulebook in force from 1 January 2026, FEES VER20.010126, charges $5,000 to apply and $5,000 a year to supervise a captive insurer. A cell company pays an additional $8,000, plus $1,000 for each cell, on application and each year, and $1,000 to add a cell later. The Rulebook does not impose a premium tax. UAE corporate tax is Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022. A Qualifying Free Zone Person pays 0 percent on Qualifying Income and 9 percent on taxable income that is not Qualifying Income. Ministerial Decision No. 229 of 2025 lists reinsurance services as a Qualifying Activity and lists insurance activities regulated under Federal Decree-Law No. 48 of 2023 as an Excluded Activity, without prejudice to reinsurance services and headquarter services to Related Parties. The FSRA does not publish a captive census, a staff count, or a licensing-day standard. Authorisation enquiries go to authorisation@adgm.com. A captive may outsource managerial functions to a captive insurance manager and not to any other party.
legislation: ADGM Financial Services Regulatory Authority Captive Insurance Business Rulebook (CIB) VER07.270426, effective 27 April 2026, and Fees Rulebook (FEES) VER20.010126, effective 1 January 2026
applicable_legislation: Captive Insurance Business Rulebook (CIB) VER07.270426, effective 27 April 2026. The first captive rulebook, CIB VER01.041015, was effective from 21 October 2015. Classes and captive-insurance management are Rules 1.2 to 1.8. Minimum capital is Rule 2.2. Annual and quarterly regulatory returns are Rule 2.3. Cell companies are Chapter 4, including the $50,000 non-cellular and cellular floors in Rules 4.2 and 4.4. Outsourcing to a captive insurance manager is Rule 5.2. Fees are Fees Rulebook (FEES) VER20.010126, Rules 3.11.3 to 3.11.7, effective 1 January 2026. ADGM was established under Federal Decree No. 15 of 2013. UAE corporate tax is Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022, as amended and published by the Ministry of Finance. Qualifying Activities and Excluded Activities for a Qualifying Free Zone Person are Ministerial Decision No. 229 of 2025.

min_capital.How the minimum is set: The minimum capital requirement is the highest of the base capital requirement, the premium-risk component, and the technical-provision risk component (CIB Rule 2.2.1). The Regulator may direct a higher minimum. A captive must also hold additional financial resources adequate for the nature, size, and complexity of its business (Rule 2.1.2).
min_capital.Class 1 captive insurer: Base capital of $150,000 (Rule 2.2.2(a)). A Class 1 captive may effect or carry out contracts of insurance only for risks related to or arising out of the business or operations of the group to which it belongs (Rule 1.4).
min_capital.Class 2 captive insurer: Base capital of $250,000, unless the Regulator sets a different amount (Rule 2.2.2(b)). Third-party gross written premium is limited to 20 percent and must arise from business or operations closely linked to the group (Rule 1.5).
min_capital.Class 3 captive insurer: Base capital of $500,000, unless the Regulator sets a different amount (Rule 2.2.2(c)). Cover is limited to persons in a similar, related, or common business, activity, trade, service, or operation, and the captive is owned by those persons or by a body corporate of which all of them are members (Rule 1.6).
min_capital.Class 4 captive insurer: Base capital of $1 million, unless the Regulator sets a different amount (Rule 2.2.2(d)). Class 4 is an entity that the Regulator decides does not meet Class 1, Class 2, or Class 3 (Rule 1.7).
min_capital.Premium-risk component: 18 percent of net written premium up to $5 million, plus 16 percent of net written premium above $5 million, for every class (Rule 2.2.3). The same formula applies to a captive cell (Rule 4.6).
min_capital.Technical-provision component: For general insurance business, 5 percent of the net claims reserve, including incurred-but-not-reported claims and claims-settlement expenses, net of expected reinsurance and other recoveries (Rule 2.2.4). For long-term insurance business, 2.5 percent of policyholder liabilities calculated using actuarial methods (Rule 2.2.5). A captive cell uses the same 5 percent and 2.5 percent components (Rules 4.7 and 4.8).
min_capital.Cell company and each active cell: A captive insurer that is a cell company must at all times hold non-cellular eligible capital of at least $50,000 (Rule 4.2.1). An active cell must maintain the higher of net cellular assets of at least $50,000 and the cell's risk-based minimum solvency requirement (Rules 4.4 and 4.5). Captive insurance business of a cell company is conducted only through captive cells (Rule 4.3).
min_capital.Form of capital: Chapter 3 sets eligible capital. A qualifying letter of credit may be included where the Regulator allows it. Rule 3.1.4 requires the letter of credit to be unconditional and irrevocable, for a fixed amount, renewable annually, and issued by a bank rated at least BBB+ by Standard & Poor's, or the equivalent by another approved rating agency, and regulated in ADGM or another jurisdiction the Regulator approves. The captive must not be required to give collateral to the bank for the letter of credit.

tax_notes: The Captive Insurance Business Rulebook does not impose a premium tax or an annual premium-tax return. UAE corporate tax is imposed by Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022. Article 3 imposes 0 percent on the portion of taxable income that does not exceed the amount set by Cabinet decision and 9 percent on taxable income above that amount. A Qualifying Free Zone Person pays 0 percent on Qualifying Income and 9 percent on taxable income that is not Qualifying Income. The Federal Tax Authority's free-zone bulletin states that a Qualifying Free Zone Person is not eligible for the 0 percent rate on the first AED 375,000 and pays 9 percent on its entire taxable income that is not Qualifying Income. Ministerial Decision No. 229 of 2025 lists reinsurance services as a Qualifying Activity. It lists insurance activities, defined as insurance operations regulated under Federal Decree-Law No. 48 of 2023, as an Excluded Activity, without prejudice to reinsurance services and to headquarter services to Related Parties. Income from an Excluded Activity is not eligible for the 0 percent rate. Whether a particular ADGM captive is a Qualifying Free Zone Person, and whether a particular contract is reinsurance, headquarter services, or an excluded insurance activity, is determined under those federal instruments and is not set by a captive class in the CIB. The 2017 ADGM captive brochure states a 0 percent tax environment until 2065. That date is not restated in CIB VER07.270426, in FEES VER20.010126, or in Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022. No captive-specific value-added-tax rate is stated in the Rulebook.
contact_name: Authorisation team, Financial Services Regulatory Authority
types_allowed: Class 1 captive insurers, limited to group risks
Class 2 captive insurers, with third-party gross written premium limited to 20 percent from closely linked business
Class 3 captive insurers, owned by persons in a similar, related, or common business
Class 4 captive insurers, as decided by the Regulator
Cell companies and class captive cells
Captive insurers whose contracts are limited to reinsurance of risks insured by the cedant
Insurance special purpose vehicles, authorised separately from the four captive classes
Captive insurance managers, authorised to administer a captive insurer

fees.licensing_incorporation: FEES Rule 3.11.3 requires an application fee of $5,000 for a financial-services permission to effect or carry out contracts of insurance as a captive insurer or as an insurance special purpose vehicle. An applicant that will operate as a cell company pays an additional application fee of $8,000 for the cell company plus $1,000 for each cell (Rule 3.11.5). After permission is granted, each later cell has an application fee of $1,000 (Rule 3.11.7). The application is not treated as submitted until the fee is paid in full (Rule 1.2.1). ADGM Registration Authority commercial-license fees are not set in the captive fee rules.
fees.annual_fees: Annual supervision fee of $5,000 for either or both of effecting and carrying out contracts of insurance as a captive insurer or an insurance special purpose vehicle (Rule 3.11.4). A cell company pays an additional annual supervision fee of $8,000 plus $1,000 for each cell (Rule 3.11.6). The initial annual fee is prorated for the months remaining in the calendar year and is due within 20 business days of the invoice. Later annual fees are due by the later of 31 January or 20 business days after the invoice (Rule 1.2.2).
fees.premium_tax_rate: No premium tax is imposed by the Captive Insurance Business Rulebook. UAE corporate tax under Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022 is 9 percent above the Cabinet threshold, and 0 percent on Qualifying Income of a Qualifying Free Zone Person. Non-qualifying income of a Qualifying Free Zone Person is taxed at 9 percent, without the AED 375,000 0 percent band. Reinsurance services are a Qualifying Activity. Insurance activities regulated under Federal Decree-Law No. 48 of 2023 are an Excluded Activity, without prejudice to reinsurance services and headquarter services to Related Parties.

annual_filing_requirements: A captive insurer submits its annual regulatory return in writing within four months of its reporting date, using the electronic prudential reporting system (CIB Rule 2.3.7). The return includes the statements the Regulator specifies. The statement by directors is signed before submission by the senior executive officer and by a director who is not the senior executive officer, and a signed hard copy is kept for at least six years. The auditor's report on the annual regulatory return, and any actuarial report prepared at the reporting date, are submitted within four months of the reporting date. The annual return, including the statement by directors, is subject to audit except where Chapter 2 or the form instructions say a form is not. Returns are in English. A cell company completes a global return and a cell return for each captive cell. Where the Regulator requires a quarterly regulatory return, it is submitted in the manner and within the time the Regulator prescribes. A captive cell that relies on an approved recourse agreement may be required to report cellular and non-cellular resources on an aggregated basis. A captive also reports group capital adequacy under PIN 6.7. Any report submitted to shareholders or policyholders for the reporting period is submitted with the annual return or as soon as practicable afterward. Assets and liabilities are recognised under IFRS except where the Rules provide a different method (Rule 6.3). A captive may outsource managerial functions only to an authorised captive insurance manager, subject to GEN 3.3 (Rule 5.2). Management systems and controls are those in GEN 3. If the captive knows or has reasonable grounds to believe that it is in breach, or may be about to be in breach, of the capital chapter, it tells the Regulator orally within one business day, confirms in writing by the next business day, and makes no distribution to shareholders or members without the Regulator's written permission. The Rules do not state an in-ADGM board-meeting requirement in the sections reviewed.

name: Alabama
summary: Alabama licenses captive insurers under the Alabama Captive Insurers Act, Code of Alabama sections 27-31B-1 to 27-31B-28, enacted as Act 2006-509. The Department of Insurance states that the Legislature passed the bill in the 2006 regular session and that Governor Bob Riley signed it. Act 2016-191, Act 2021-162, and Act 2026-486 have amended the chapter. The Department administers the Act. A captive may be a pure, agency, association, industrial insured, protected cell, incorporated cell, reinsurance, or special purpose financial captive, or a captive risk retention group, and it may be formed as a stock, mutual, nonprofit, limited liability, or reciprocal insurer. A branch captive is an alien captive licensed for Alabama operations and is a pure captive for those operations unless the commissioner permits otherwise. Unimpaired paid-in capital and surplus is at least $250,000 for a pure captive or a protected cell captive, $500,000 for an agency, association, or industrial insured captive, $1,000,000 for a reinsurance captive or a risk retention group, and $250,000 for a branch captive. The commissioner may set another actuarially supported amount for a pure, agency, association, protected cell, or risk retention group captive. A reciprocal maintains free surplus of $1,000,000. Section 27-31B-6 does not state a separate dollar floor for a special purpose financial captive or for an individual incorporated cell. Direct premium tax is 0.4 percent, 0.3 percent, 0.2 percent, and 0.075 percent on successive $20 million bands. Assumed-reinsurance tax is 0.225 percent, 0.150 percent, 0.050 percent, and 0.025 percent. The minimum is $5,000 and the maximum is $100,000. No tax is due for a calendar year in which the captive writes no premiums. The minimum is prorated if the captive is licensed or surrenders its license for less than a full year. Rule 482-1-138-.20, effective 1 January 2022, sets the adjusted application fee at $240 and the initial and annual license fee at $360. The Department's fee schedule also lists a $200 application examination fee. The commissioner may issue a provisional license for not more than 60 days. A temporary moratorium on new captive and domestic risk-retention-group filings ended on 30 June 2026. The Department's 1 July 2026 bulletin says new filings are accepted and processed in the ordinary course. The Department does not publish a captive census or a staff count. The captive tax form names the Examination Division at ExaminationDivision@insurance.alabama.gov.
legislation: Alabama Captive Insurers Act, Code of Alabama Title 27, Chapter 31B, sections 27-31B-1 to 27-31B-28, and Alabama Administrative Code Chapter 482-1-138
applicable_legislation: Chapter 31B originated in Act 2006-509. The code history of the licensing section cites Act 2008-391, Act 2016-191, Act 2021-162, and Act 2026-486. Capital and surplus are section 27-31B-6. The statutory fee amounts are section 27-31B-4. The adjusted fees in force are Rule 482-1-138-.20, effective 1 January 2022, adopted under sections 27-31B-4 and 41-1-11. Reports are section 27-31B-9, amended by Act 2016-191 and Act 2026-486. Examinations are section 27-31B-10. Premium tax is section 27-31B-16, amended by Act 2016-191. Protected cell captives are sections 27-31B-22 to 27-31B-25. Captive risk retention groups are also subject to section 27-31B-28, and Rule 482-1-138-.17.1 lists additional Title 27 chapters that apply to them. Chapter 482-1-138 was new on 1 August 2006 and effective 11 August 2006, and later rules in the chapter were revised through 2021.

min_capital.Pure captive: Not less than $250,000, or another amount determined by the commissioner and actuarially supported by a feasibility study (section 27-31B-6(a)(1)).
min_capital.Agency captive: Not less than $500,000, or another amount determined by the commissioner and actuarially supported by a feasibility study (section 27-31B-6(a)(2)).
min_capital.Association captive: Not less than $500,000, or another amount determined by the commissioner and actuarially supported by a feasibility study (section 27-31B-6(a)(3)).
min_capital.Reinsurance captive: Not less than $1,000,000 (section 27-31B-6(a)(5)). A reinsurance captive only assumes risks from an insurer or reinsurer approved or licensed in Alabama or in a foreign or alien jurisdiction the commissioner approves, and it assumes those risks on a funds-withheld basis or another basis the commissioner accepts (section 27-31B-2(32)).
min_capital.Protected cell captive: Not less than $250,000, or another amount determined by the commissioner and actuarially supported by a feasibility study (section 27-31B-6(a)(6)). Section 27-31B-6 does not state a separate dollar floor for an individual protected cell or for an incorporated cell. The sponsors provide the minimum capital and surplus (section 27-31B-2(29)).
min_capital.Branch captive: Not less than $250,000 (section 27-31B-6(a)(7)). As security for liabilities attributable to the branch operations, the commissioner may require collateral equal to the net loss reserves on branch business plus other insurance liabilities the commissioner determines, maintained in a manner acceptable to the commissioner (section 27-31B-6(e)). A branch captive is a pure captive for its Alabama operations unless the commissioner permits otherwise (section 27-31B-2(7)).
min_capital.Risk retention group: Not less than $1,000,000, or another amount determined by the commissioner and actuarially supported by a feasibility study (section 27-31B-6(a)(8)).
min_capital.Reciprocal captive: Free surplus of $1,000,000, notwithstanding the amounts in subsection (a) (section 27-31B-6(b)).
min_capital.Special purpose financial captive: Section 27-31B-2(33) defines a special purpose financial captive as a captive that has received a certificate of authority for the limited purposes provided in the chapter. Section 27-31B-6 does not state a separate dollar floor for that type.
min_capital.Additional capital and form: The commissioner may prescribe additional capital and surplus based on the type, volume, and nature of the business (section 27-31B-6(c)). Capital and surplus may be cash, cash equivalents, a surplus note, securities meeting section 27-6-3, or, if the commissioner approves, a clean, irrevocable, and unconditional letter of credit issued by an Alabama-chartered bank or a Federal Reserve member bank. No assets of the captive may be pledged or encumbered for payment of the letter of credit (section 27-31B-6(d)). A captive may be capitalized with a surplus note on terms the section permits.

tax_notes: Section 27-31B-16 requires the tax by 1 March, paid to the commissioner. Direct premiums, after return premiums and policyholder dividends or premium deposits returned or credited, are taxed at four-tenths of one percent on the first $20 million, three-tenths of one percent on the next $20 million, two-tenths of one percent on the next $20 million, and seventy-five thousandths of one percent thereafter. Annuity considerations are not taxed. Assumed-reinsurance premiums are taxed at 0.225 percent on the first $20 million, 0.150 percent on the next $20 million, 0.050 percent on the next $20 million, and 0.025 percent thereafter. Reinsurance tax does not apply to risks taxed on a direct basis, or to a qualifying assumption of loss reserves and other liabilities of another insurer under common ownership and control that is part of a plan to discontinue that insurer. If the calculated tax is under $5,000, the tax is $5,000. The aggregate tax may not exceed $100,000. Because the $100,000 maximum is reached inside the second direct-premium band, the 0.2 percent and 0.075 percent direct bands do not increase the tax once that maximum applies. The Department's tax form, revised 6 September 2024, states the direct schedule as 0.4 percent up to $20 million and then $80,000 plus 0.3 percent of the excess, not to exceed $100,000. For a protected cell captive, the $5,000 minimum applies to the company as a whole and not to each protected cell. The maximum paid by a protected cell captive is the aggregate of the tax liabilities of each protected cell, and the maximum attributed to any one protected cell captive is $100,000. Examination expenses under section 27-31B-10 and business-privilege tax paid under section 40-14A-22 are credits for the calendar year in which they were paid. A credit that would reduce the tax below zero produces a tax of zero and is not carried forward. The premium tax is all of the tax collectible under Alabama law from a captive, except business-privilege tax and ad valorem taxes on real and personal property used to produce income. The chapter does not state the business-privilege-tax rate. Two or more captives under common ownership and control are taxed as one captive. For stock corporations, common ownership and control is direct or indirect ownership of 80 percent or more of the outstanding voting stock. For mutual corporations, it is direct or indirect ownership of 80 percent or more of the surplus and the voting power. Branch tax applies only to branch business. If the captive writes no premiums during the calendar year, the tax is not applicable. If a captive is licensed for less than a full year and the calculated tax is below the minimum, the minimum is 100 percent, 75 percent, 50 percent, or 25 percent according to whether the license date falls on or before 31 March, from 1 April to 30 June, from 1 July to 30 September, or from 1 October to 31 December. A surrender is prorated at 25 percent, 50 percent, 75 percent, or 100 percent on those same bands. The Department's tax form states the same rates, the $360 renewal fee, the proration, and the credits.
contact_name: Examination Division, Alabama Department of Insurance
types_allowed: Protected cell captive insurance companies and protected cells
Incorporated cell captive insurance companies and incorporated cells
Captives formed as stock insurers, mutual insurers, nonprofit corporations, limited liability companies, or reciprocal insurers

fees.licensing_incorporation: Section 27-31B-4 states a $200 fee for filing the license application and a $300 license fee for the initial license and each annual renewal. Rule 482-1-138-.20, effective 1 January 2022, adjusts those amounts under section 41-1-11 to a $240 application fee and a $360 initial and annual license fee. The Department's captive application fee schedule, citing Act 2021-162 effective 1 July 2021, lists a $240 application fee and a $200 application examination fee, both paid with the initial online application, and a $360 fee paid on receipt of the tentative-approval email. The commissioner may also charge the reasonable cost of outside legal, financial, and examination services under section 27-2-25. Secretary of State organization fees are not set in Chapter 31B.
fees.annual_fees: Annual license renewal fee of $360 under Rule 482-1-138-.20 and the Department's 6 September 2024 captive tax form. Section 27-31B-3(f) states that a license authorizes business until 1 April and may be renewed. The renewal fee is reported on line 5 of the captive fee and tax return and is paid with the premium tax by 1 March.
fees.premium_tax_rate: Direct premiums: 0.4 percent, 0.3 percent, 0.2 percent, and 0.075 percent on successive $20 million bands. The Department's tax form states the direct calculation as 0.4 percent up to $20 million and $80,000 plus 0.3 percent of the excess, not to exceed $100,000. Assumed reinsurance: 0.225 percent, 0.150 percent, 0.050 percent, and 0.025 percent on successive $20 million bands. Annual minimum $5,000, prorated if the captive is licensed or surrenders for less than a full year and the calculated tax is below the minimum. Annual maximum $100,000. For a protected cell captive the minimum applies to the company as a whole, and the company maximum is $100,000. No tax if no premiums are written. Due 1 March. Examination expenses and business-privilege tax are credits and cannot reduce the tax below zero.

annual_filing_requirements: Before 1 March, each captive submits a report of its financial condition verified by the oath of two executive officers (section 27-31B-9). Reporting uses statutory accounting principles unless the commissioner approves generally accepted accounting principles, except as section 27-31B-6 provides. An association captive, and an industrial insured captive insuring an industrial insured group under section 27-31B-2(19)b, files in the form required by section 27-3-26. A risk retention group files in that form and complies with the casualty-insurer filing requirements. The Department's annual-statement page assigns the NAIC property-and-casualty blank to association captives and to industrial insured captives of a section 27-31B-2(19)b group, the pure or industrial-insured captive statement to pure captives and to industrial insured captives of a section 27-31B-2(19)a group, and the NAIC protected-cell blank to sponsored captives. A pure captive, or an industrial insured captive of a section 27-31B-2(19)a group, may be allowed to report on a fiscal year. The report is then due 60 days after fiscal year-end, and pages 1, 2, 3, and 5 of the pure or industrial-insured statement for the calendar year-end are still filed before 1 March. A branch captive files, 60 days after fiscal year-end, copies of the reports required where the alien captive is formed. The commissioner may waive the captive annual statement for business written in the alien jurisdiction if the domiciliary report is adequate. On or before 30 June, an audited statement of financial condition for the preceding calendar year is prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States and includes the independent certified public accountant's report, a balance sheet, an income statement, a statement of cash flows, a statement of changes in capital and surplus, and notes (section 27-31B-9(e)). An annual actuarial certification of loss and loss-expense reserves, by a qualified actuary as defined in the NAIC property-and-casualty statement instructions and approved by the commissioner, is filed with the 1 March report. Rule 482-1-138-.04 also requires the audit by 30 June and states that a captive other than a captive risk retention group, with direct premiums under $2,200,000 and fewer than 1,000 policyholders or certificate holders, or with assumed premiums of $2,200,000 or less, may apply for an annual exemption from the audit. The exemption is renewed annually. A captive risk retention group may apply for a hardship exemption from the audit, and that exemption does not remove the reserve certification. The board of directors or managers, or a reciprocal's subscribers' advisory committee, meets at least once each year in Alabama. The principal place of business is in Alabama, or the branch maintains a place of business for its branch operations. A registered agent is appointed. The captive owns an account at an Alabama bank or credit union with a physical location the commissioner approves, or at a veteran-related financial institution the commissioner approves. It employs or contracts with a captive manager, an independent certified public accountant, and an actuary, each meeting the commissioner's standards. The manager, or the manager's officers and directors, may not serve as president except where the captive contracts with its parent, an affiliate, or a controlled unaffiliated business for management. Section 27-31B-10 requires an examination at least once in three years and whenever the commissioner determines it to be prudent. On application, the commissioner may enlarge the period to five years if the captive has a comprehensive annual audit of a satisfactory scope by approved independent auditors. The examination is at the captive's cost under section 27-2-25. A branch examination is limited to branch business and branch operations if the branch annually provides a certificate of compliance from its home jurisdiction. The commissioner may issue a provisional license for not more than 60 days after a complete application, payment of the fees, and a preliminary finding that the persons who will control and manage the captive are acceptable. The chapter as published does not contain a dormant-captive status. Bulletins 2025-01 and 2025-05 imposed a temporary moratorium on new captive and domestic risk-retention-group filings. The Department's 1 July 2026 bulletin terminated that moratorium effective immediately and states that new filings are accepted and processed in the ordinary course. The captives page still links the earlier moratorium bulletins.

captive_administrator.name: Examination Division, Alabama Department of Insurance

licensing_speed: Section 27-31B-3(g) allows the commissioner to issue a provisional license for not more than 60 days when the public interest will be served, after a complete application, payment of the licensure fees, and a preliminary finding that the persons who will control and manage the captive are acceptable. The provisional license ends automatically if the regular process is not completed within 60 days. The Department does not publish a standard number of days for an ordinary license. The 1 July 2026 bulletin states that new filings are accepted and processed in the ordinary course.

name: Alberta
summary: Alberta enacted dedicated captive insurance legislation under the Captive Insurance Companies Act (SA 2021, c. C-2.4), which came into force on July 1, 2022, making it the second Canadian province with a standalone captive statute. Administered by the Alberta Superintendent of Insurance (Treasury Board and Finance), the regime authorizes pure, association, and sophisticated insured captives—formed as either corporations or limited partnerships—as well as redomestication of foreign captives. Driven by strong demand from the energy, natural resource, and commercial sectors, along with Canada's lowest provincial corporate income tax rate (8%) and streamlined 6-week licensing, Alberta has rapidly expanded its captive insurance sector. The Superintendent's Captive Insurance Company Licensing Guide, updated November 7, 2025, states that captives may underwrite all classes of insurance except automobile insurance for basic coverage and surety insurance. Canadian Underwriter reported on October 30, 2026 that Hub International senior vice-president Angela Iannetta said Alberta's rules now allow a captive to insure a surety program.
legislation: Captive Insurance Companies Act, SA 2021, c. C-2.4 (in force July 1, 2022) & Captive Insurance Companies Regulation, Alta. Reg. 100/2022
applicable_legislation: Captive Insurance Companies Act (SA 2021, c. C-2.4); Captive Insurance Companies Regulation (Alta. Reg. 100/2022); Captive Insurance Companies (Prescribed Enactments) Regulation (Alta. Reg. 103/2022); Fees Under the Captive Insurance Companies Act Order (Ministerial Order 14/2022); Classes of Insurance Regulation (Alta. Reg. 144/2011); Recovery of Insurance Administration Costs Regulation (Alta. Reg. 102/2022); Insurance Enforcement and Administration Regulation (Alta. Reg. 101/2022); Business Corporations Act (RSA 2000, c. B-9); Partnership Act (RSA 2000, c. P-3); Alberta Corporate Tax Act (RSA 2000, c. A-15).

min_capital.Pure Captive: CAD 250,000 minimum base capital (or greater of 20% of first CAD 5M Net Insurance Revenue + 10% over CAD 5M, or 15% of net Liabilities for Incurred Claims for P&C; subject to Superintendent's risk-based determination)
min_capital.Association Captive: CAD 500,000 minimum base capital (or greater of formulaic revenue/claims thresholds or actuary-proposed risk-based amount; subject to Superintendent's determination)
min_capital.Sophisticated Insured Captive: CAD 500,000 minimum base capital (insureds must demonstrate insurance expertise and pay at least CAD 500,000 in aggregate annual premiums; subject to Superintendent's determination)

tax_notes: Subject to federal and provincial corporate income tax (8% Alberta general corporate tax rate) and Alberta insurance premiums tax under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act (3% on life, accident and sickness insurance; 4% on property, casualty and other insurance contracts on Alberta risks).
contact_name: Erin O'Neill, Alberta Superintendent of Insurance

name: Anguilla
summary: Anguilla licenses insurers under the Insurance Act, R.S.A. c. I16, administered by the Anguilla Financial Services Commission. Act 6/2004 came into force on 1 October 2004. The revised edition published by the Commission shows the law as at 15 December 2014 and consolidates Act 6/2004, Act 3/2006, and Act 4/2013. The dollar in the Act is a United States dollar. Class B licences are the offshore and captive classes. Issued and paid-up capital is at least $200,000 for an unrestricted Class B licence, $100,000 for a general Class B licence, $100,000 for an association Class B licence, $25,000 for a group Class B licence, and $10,000 for a single Class B licence. The Commission may order a higher amount. The Insurance (Amendment) Act, 2018, Act No. 6/2018, added a producer affiliated reinsurance company licence. That licence is restricted to reinsurance and requires issued and paid-up capital of at least $5,000. Act No. 10/2018 replaced the definition so that the ultimate beneficial owners are the same as those of, or affiliated with, the producer. The Commission's Director's Report for 2023 states that 47 captive insurers held licences at 31 December 2023, that no new captive licences were granted in 2023, and that there were 15 licence cancellations, down from 62 at the beginning of 2023. The report does not split that count by licence class, and no later annual report is published on the reports page. The Insurance (Amendment) Regulations, 2018, set the current fees. A Class B application is $1,500 for an unrestricted licence, $1,000 for a general licence, and $750 for an association, group, or single licence or for a producer affiliated reinsurance company. The annual licence fee is $4,000 for an unrestricted licence carrying on general and long-term business, $3,000 for an unrestricted long-term licence, $3,000 for a general licence, $2,500 for an association, group, or single licence, and $750 for a producer affiliated reinsurance company in each calendar year after the year of grant. Section 6 requires the annual fee by 15 January. The Act does not impose a premium tax. Section 18(4) exempts contracts executed for the foreign insurance business of a licensed insurer from stamp duty. A fast-track process published by the Commission licenses a captive or producer affiliated reinsurance company within one business day of a complete submission by an approved insurance manager, provided the company has been incorporated. No ordinary turnaround, staff count, or captive association is published.
legislation: Insurance Act, R.S.A. c. I16, as amended by the Insurance (Amendment) Act, 2018, Act No. 6/2018, and the Insurance (Amendment) (No. 2) Act, 2018, Act No. 10/2018, and the Insurance Regulations, R.R.A. I16-1, as amended by the Insurance (Amendment) Regulations, 2018
applicable_legislation: Insurance Act, R.S.A. c. I16. Act 6/2004 came into force on 1 October 2004. The revised edition on the Commission website shows the law as at 15 December 2014 and consolidates Act 6/2004, Act 3/2006 in force 27 March 2006, and Act 4/2013 in force 25 September 2013. That edition does not include the 2018 amendments. Classes and minimum issued and paid-up capital are section 3(1). The Commission may order a higher amount under section 3(4). Trustee ownership is section 4. The annual fee date is section 6. Accounts, the insurance-manager requirement, and the solvency margin are section 8. Class B annual returns are section 10(3). A company must have at least two directors under section 13. Stamp-duty exemption for foreign insurance contracts is section 18(4). The Insurance (Amendment) Act, 2018, Act No. 6/2018, was passed by the House of Assembly on 10 July 2018 and assented to on 13 July 2018. It inserts the producer affiliated reinsurance company definition and section 3(1)(g), exempts that company from the audit requirement in section 8(5), and requires its return within three months of financial year-end. The Insurance (Amendment) (No. 2) Act, 2018, Act No. 10/2018, was passed by the House on 14 September 2018 and replaces the definition. Fees are Schedule 6 of the Insurance Regulations as substituted by the Insurance (Amendment) Regulations, 2018, R.A. 16/2018. Solvency margins in the Commission's guidance notes were made on 1 March 2008 under the power cited in those notes. The letter-of-credit guidelines were approved by the Board on 10 December 2013.

min_capital.Class B unrestricted: Issued and paid-up capital of at least US$200,000 (section 3(1)(b)). The licence permits any foreign insurance business, including long-term foreign insurance business. The Act defines a dollar as a dollar of the United States.
min_capital.Class B general: Issued and paid-up capital of at least US$100,000 (section 3(1)(c)). The licence permits general foreign insurance business and not long-term foreign insurance business.
min_capital.Class B association: Issued and paid-up capital of at least US$100,000 (section 3(1)(d), as amended by Act 3/2006). The insurer has two or more owners. It may carry on no more than 50 percent of its foreign insurance business, measured by net premiums written, or 100 percent of its reinsurance business, with persons who are not owners of the insurer or its affiliates. The Commission's insurance page states the 50 percent net-premium limit and does not restate the reinsurance limb.
min_capital.Class B group: Issued and paid-up capital of at least US$25,000 (section 3(1)(e)). The business is with a single owner, that owner's affiliates, and employees of the owner or its affiliates, and may include long-term foreign insurance business.
min_capital.Class B single: Issued and paid-up capital of at least US$10,000 (section 3(1)(f)). The business is with the sole owner, if a company, and may include long-term foreign insurance business. The Commission's insurance page also describes this licence as available to a trust, for business with the beneficial owners. Section 4 allows the shares of a licensed insurer to be owned by trustees of a trust, including a purpose trust, with the Commission's approval.
min_capital.Producer affiliated reinsurance company: Issued and paid-up capital of at least US$5,000 (Insurance (Amendment) Act, 2018, section 3, inserting section 3(1)(g)). The licence permits foreign insurance business, including long-term foreign insurance business, but only as reinsurance. The Commission's procedure of 6 July 2018 requires proof that the paid-up capital has been deposited in a bank account in the company's name within 30 days after the licence is granted.
min_capital.Higher capital and solvency margin: The Commission may order a licensee to increase its paid-up capital, having regard to the nature and extent of the business (section 3(4)). The insurer must report immediately if its net worth falls below the required paid-up capital (section 3(6)). Section 8(13) requires a solvency margin at least equal to the margin specified in regulations or by the Commission. The Commission's guidance notes made on 1 March 2008 state that, for an insurer other than one carrying on long-term business, the margin is the greater of the section 3(1) paid-up capital and a premium test: 20 percent of net retained annual premium where that premium does not exceed US$5,000,000, or US$1,000,000 plus 10 percent of the excess where it does. For long-term business the notes require at least the section 3(1) paid-up capital. An insurer writing both maintains the aggregate.
min_capital.Form of capital: Section 3(1) requires issued and paid-up capital. The Commission's letter-of-credit guidelines, approved by the Board on 10 December 2013, state that the Commission's preference is cash paid for fully paid-up shares. Pending a review of the Act, the Commission will accept a letter of credit as a component of paid-up capital at the initial licensing of a captive insurer if the letter of credit is irrevocable, is issued for the Commission's benefit by a bank licensed in Anguilla with a short-term debt rating of at least A-1 from Standard & Poor's or P-1 from Moody's, is delivered to the Commission before the licence is issued, and follows the stated form. The guidelines do not treat a letter of credit as issued share capital under the Companies Act.

tax_notes: The Insurance Act does not impose a premium tax or an annual premium-tax return. Section 18(4) provides that contracts of insurance executed for or in connection with the foreign insurance business of a licensed insurer are exempt from stamp duty. Section 18(1) provides that a company licensed under the Act is not required to be licensed under the Trades, Businesses, Occupations and Professions Licensing Act. The Commission's Director's Report for 2023 states that the Goods and Services Tax Act, which took effect on 1 July 2022 and introduced taxes on insurance premiums, was amended in late 2023 to repeal and remove taxes applicable to the sale of insurance products effective 7 December 2023. No corporate income-tax rate for a Class B insurer or a producer affiliated reinsurance company is stated in the Insurance Act, the Insurance Regulations, or the Commission's insurance pages reviewed. The regulatory charge that is published is the licence fee in Schedule 6, not a premium-tax rate.
contact_name: Anguilla Financial Services Commission
types_allowed: Class B unrestricted insurers, writing any foreign insurance business, including long-term business
Class B general insurers, writing general foreign insurance business and not long-term business
Class B association insurers, with two or more owners
Class B group insurers, writing for a single owner, its affiliates, and their employees
Class B single insurers, writing for the sole owner
Producer affiliated reinsurance companies licensed under section 3(1)(g)
Insurers whose shares are owned by trustees of a trust approved under section 4

fees.licensing_incorporation: Schedule 6, as substituted by the Insurance (Amendment) Regulations, 2018, charges a non-refundable application fee of US$1,500 for a Class B licence under section 3(1)(b), US$1,000 for a Class B licence under section 3(1)(c), US$750 for a Class B licence under section 3(1)(d), (e), or (f), and US$750 for a producer affiliated reinsurance company licence under section 3(1)(g). An insurance manager's application fee is US$1,000. The Commission's procedure approved on 6 July 2018 states that the US$750 producer affiliated reinsurance company application fee includes the first year's annual licence fee, and that the company must be incorporated and the fee paid before the licence is granted. Company-incorporation fees payable to the registry are not set in Schedule 6. An insurance manager approved to use the fast-track process pays a separate non-refundable application fee of US$500 and an approval fee of US$2,000, then US$2,000 a year, in addition to its own licence fee.
fees.annual_fees: Section 6 requires every current licensee to pay the prescribed annual fee on or before 15 January. Schedule 6, as substituted in 2018, charges an annual licence fee of US$3,000 for a section 3(1)(b) licence for long-term business, US$4,000 for a section 3(1)(b) licence for general and long-term business, US$3,000 for a section 3(1)(c) general licence, and US$2,500 for a section 3(1)(d), (e), or (f) licence. A producer affiliated reinsurance company pays US$750 for each calendar year following the calendar year in which the licence is granted. If a licence other than that producer affiliated reinsurance company annual charge is granted on or after 1 July, half of the relevant prescribed licence fee is payable at grant. An insurance manager's annual licence fee is US$2,000. The 2018 schedule does not restate the late-payment percentages that appeared in the earlier schedule.
fees.premium_tax_rate: No premium tax is imposed by the Insurance Act. Foreign insurance contracts of a licensed insurer are exempt from stamp duty under section 18(4). The Commission's 2023 Director's Report states that goods and services tax on the sale of insurance products was removed effective 7 December 2023. No corporate income-tax rate for these licensees is published in the Act or the Commission materials reviewed. The standing regulatory charge is the Schedule 6 licence fee.

annual_filing_requirements: A Class B insurer furnishes an annual return within six months of the end of its financial year, including the audited annual accounts required by section 8(5), a certificate of compliance under section 8(4), and such other information as the Commission requires in order to be satisfied of the insurer's solvency and compliance (section 10(3)). Annual accounts are prepared on generally accepted accounting principles acceptable to the Commission and are audited by an independent auditor the Commission approves, unless the Commission exempts the insurer in writing. A producer affiliated reinsurance company is excluded from that audit requirement. It prepares and furnishes, within three months of the end of its financial year, annual accounts in a form acceptable to the Commission, a certificate of compliance, and a solvency calculation in a form acceptable to the Commission. It must obtain the Commission's prior approval for a change in the primary insurer. The Commission's guideline of 30 October 2018 treats a primary insurer as acceptable if it has an A.M. Best financial-strength rating of B+ or higher, or an equivalent rating the Commission accepts, is licensed and supervised in a home jurisdiction the Commission accepts, and is in good standing with its home regulator. The annual licence fee is due by 15 January under section 6. Every insurer other than an approved external insurer, or an insurer that maintains its principal office and staff permanently in Anguilla, appoints an insurance manager and keeps full records at a designated principal office in Anguilla or another location the Commission approves. A company has at least two directors, and a director or senior officer is not appointed without the Commission's prior approval unless the Commission exempts the licensee in writing. A Class B insurer may not carry on domestic business except where that business is a minor part of the international risk of a policyholder whose main activities are outside Anguilla, and it applies to the Commission in writing before doing so. The Act does not state an in-Anguilla board-meeting requirement in the sections reviewed. The Commission publishes licence issuance, revocation, and suspension in the Gazette.

captive_administrator.name: Anguilla Financial Services Commission

licensing_speed: The Commission's fast-track procedure for captive insurers and producer affiliated reinsurance companies says the Commission will license the applicant within one business day of receiving a complete submission from an insurance manager approved to use the process, provided the applicant has been incorporated. The submission, including the application fee and licence fee, goes to applications@afsc.ai. The licence is approved in reliance on that submission, and the Commission may suspend or revoke it if the submission does not comply with the licensing guidelines. The Act and the published procedure do not state a number of days for an application that is not on the fast track.

name: Arizona
summary: Arizona's Captive Insurance Division, in the Department of Insurance and Financial Institutions, licenses captives under Arizona Revised Statutes sections 20-1098 through 20-1098.24. The division states that the captive statute took effect in 2002. A captive may be pure, group, agency, or protected cell, and may be formed as a stock insurer, limited liability company, mutual, reciprocal, or nonprofit. A group captive is an association captive, an industry group captive, or a risk retention group. The statute also provides for branch captives and for dormant captives. Minimum unimpaired paid-in capital and surplus is $250,000 for a pure or protected cell captive and $500,000 for a group, agency, or reciprocal captive. A pure or group captive that transacts only reinsurance holds half of the applicable amount. A dormant captive with a certificate of dormancy holds $125,000. Fees under section 20-167(F) are in lieu of premium tax and other state and local taxes, except taxes on real and tangible personal property located in Arizona, transaction privilege and use taxes, and the section 20-224 premium tax that an agency captive owes on specified life and disability policies to the extent it exceeds those fees. As of 30 June 2026 the division counted 209 captives: 181 pure including reinsurers, 6 protected cell, 5 industry group, 1 association, 4 agency, 12 risk retention groups, and no branch captives. Its growth table lists 14 licenses issued in 2026 beside that cumulative count of 209. The director must approve or deny an application within 30 days after deeming it complete. The governing body meets at least once a year in Arizona, and the captive keeps its principal place of business, books and records, and an Arizona manager in the state.
legislation: Arizona Revised Statutes sections 20-1098 through 20-1098.24 (captive insurers)
applicable_legislation: Arizona Revised Statutes sections 20-1098 through 20-1098.24. Definitions are section 20-1098. Licensing, permitted business, the in-state meeting and principal-place requirements, and the 30-day decision are section 20-1098.01. Minimum capital and surplus are section 20-1098.03. Protected cells are section 20-1098.05. The annual report and audit are section 20-1098.07. The fee-in-lieu and premium-tax rule is section 20-1098.17. Dormancy is section 20-1098.24. Certificate of authority fees for captive insurers are set by the director under section 20-167(F). The Captive Insurance Division states that the captive statute's effective date is 2002. A session-law citation for the original enactment was not retrieved, so 2002 is the effective year the division publishes and is not recorded here as a separately verified enactment year.

min_capital.Pure: At least $250,000 of unimpaired paid-in capital and surplus in combination (A.R.S. section 20-1098.03(A)(1)). The division publishes the same floor.
min_capital.Group: At least $500,000 (section 20-1098.03(A)(2)). A group captive insurer is an association captive, an industry group captive, or a risk retention group (section 20-1098(16)). The division lists association and industry group captives, and risk retention groups, at $500,000.
min_capital.Protected cell: At least $250,000 (section 20-1098.03(A)(4)). The division publishes the same floor.
min_capital.Reciprocal: At least $500,000 for a captive insurer organized as a reciprocal insurer (section 20-1098.03(A)(5)).
min_capital.Pure or group, reinsurance only: One-half of the applicable pure or group amount (section 20-1098.03(A)(6)). The division states that pure reinsurers hold 50 percent of the indicated amounts.
min_capital.Dormant: A dormant captive insurer that has been issued a certificate of dormancy maintains unimpaired paid-in capital and surplus of at least $125,000 (section 20-1098.24(B)(1)). A risk retention group is excluded from the dormant-captive definition.
min_capital.Branch: The division lists branch captive insurers as a type and counted none at 30 June 2026. Section 20-1098.03 does not state a separate dollar floor for a branch captive.
min_capital.Form and additional capital: The statutory minimum is cash or an irrevocable and unconditional letter of credit with an evergreen clause, payable to, filed with, and held by the director (section 20-1098.03(B)). The director may prescribe additional capital and surplus based on the type, volume, and nature of insurance (section 20-1098.03(C)).

tax_notes: A.R.S. section 20-1098.17 provides that the captive fees paid under section 20-167(F) are payment in full and in lieu of all other state, county, district, municipal, and school taxes, licenses, and excises, except a tax on real and tangible personal property located in Arizona, the transaction privilege tax and use tax under title 42, chapter 5, articles 1 and 4, and transaction privilege and use taxes imposed by a county, city, or town. An agency captive insurer that insures the life or disability risks specified in section 20-1098.01(A)(3)(b) pays the premium tax prescribed in section 20-224 on those policies to the extent it exceeds the fees paid under section 20-167. The Captive Insurance Division states that Arizona has no insurance premium tax. The annual regulatory charge published by the division is the flat license renewal fee, not a premium-tax rate.
contact_name: Victoria E. Fimea, J.D., Chief Captive Analyst
types_allowed: Pure captive insurers, including pure reinsurers
Captive insurers organized as reciprocal insurers
Dormant captive insurers holding a certificate of dormancy, other than risk retention groups

fees.licensing_incorporation: DIFI's captive payment page lists an original insurer license application total of $1,175 and an original per-cell application of $1,000. The division's fee table lists a $100 examiners' revolving-fund deposit, a $75 charter-document filing fee, and a $60 articles of incorporation or organization fee payable to the Arizona Corporation Commission. The payment page also lists a $200 license-amendment fee and a $30 amended-charter fee. Fees are nonrefundable. The applicant may also be billed for outside specialists used in the review. Section 20-1098.01(J) requires the nonrefundable issuance fee prescribed under section 20-167.
fees.annual_fees: Captive insurer annual license renewal of $5,500, and a protected-cell annual renewal of $2,500, as published by the division and on its payment page. The renewal fee is paid not earlier than 1 July and not later than 1 September (section 20-1098.01(J)). A certificate of dormancy is renewed every five years; the statute points that fee to section 20-167 and the division page does not publish a separate dormancy amount.
fees.premium_tax_rate: No generally applicable captive premium tax. Fees under section 20-167(F) are in lieu of other state and local taxes, subject to the property-tax, transaction-privilege-tax, use-tax, and agency-captive exceptions in section 20-1098.17. The standing annual regulatory charge is the $5,500 license renewal, plus $2,500 for each protected cell.

annual_filing_requirements: Not later than 90 days after the end of its fiscal year, a captive insurer submits a report of its financial condition verified by the oath of two executive officers. The report may use generally accepted accounting principles unless the director requires statutory accounting principles, with any modifications the director requires (A.R.S. section 20-1098.07(A)). Financial statements are audited by an independent certified public accountant unless the director determines that an audit is not necessary, and the audit opinion is filed not later than six months after fiscal year-end. Unless the director grants an exemption, the annual report meets the applicable life and health, property and casualty, or NAIC health actuarial requirements. A protected cell captive also files an accounting of each protected cell with the annual report. A branch captive files, within 60 days after its fiscal year-end, the reports required by its home jurisdiction. A dormant captive with a certificate of dormancy files a verified financial-condition report within 90 days after fiscal year-end. The license renewal fee is due between 1 July and 1 September. The division states that an exemption from the annual actuarial certification and audit may apply to small captive insurers, and that there is no routine statutory examination for pure captive insurers.

captive_administrator.name: Victoria E. Fimea, J.D., Chief Captive Analyst, Captive Insurance Division

licensing_speed: The director shall approve or deny an application within 30 days after the director deems the application complete (A.R.S. section 20-1098.01(L)).

regulator.name: Arizona Department of Insurance and Financial Institutions, Captive Insurance Division
regulator.address: 100 North 15th Avenue, Suite 261, Phoenix, AZ 85007-2630

name: Arkansas
summary: Arkansas licenses captive insurers under Arkansas Code Title 23, Chapter 63, Subchapter 16, enacted by Act 1391 of 2001 and administered by the Arkansas Insurance Department. Act 554 of 2025, Senate Bill 237, became Act 554 on 14 April 2025. The Department's Bulletin 9-2025 states that an act of the 2025 regular session without an emergency clause or another stated effective date took effect on 5 August 2025. Act 554 removed the requirement that an association have been in continuous existence for at least one year, authorized a provisional licence, lowered several capital and surplus floors, set a seven-year examination cycle for a pure captive, and added a premium-tax credit for qualifying Arkansas wages. Unimpaired paid-in capital is $300,000 for a producer reinsurance captive, $100,000 for a pure captive, $250,000 for an association or industrial insured captive incorporated as a stock insurer, $100,000 for a sponsored captive, and, for a special purpose captive, an amount the commissioner determines after reviewing the business plan but not less than $125,000. Unimpaired surplus is $300,000 for a producer reinsurance captive, $100,000 for a pure captive, $250,000 for an association or industrial insured stock captive, $500,000 for an association or industrial insured mutual captive, $100,000 for a sponsored captive, and not less than $125,000 for a special purpose captive. The Department publishes the same dollar floors. Direct premium tax is 0.250 percent, 0.150 percent, and 0.050 percent on successive bands, and assumed-reinsurance tax is 0.225 percent, 0.150 percent, 0.050 percent, and 0.025 percent. The annual minimum is $5,000 and the annual maximum is $100,000. The application fee is $200 and the licence and annual renewal fee is $300. A dormant captive maintains at least $25,000 of unimpaired paid-in capital and surplus and is not liable for the premium tax. The Department does not publish a captive census, a staff count, or a standard number of days for an ordinary licence. The published contact is the Finance Division at Insurance.Finance@Arkansas.gov.
legislation: Arkansas Code Title 23, Chapter 63, Subchapter 16, Licensing and Regulation of Captive Insurers, and 23 CAR Part 29
applicable_legislation: Subchapter 16 was enacted by Act 1391 of 2001, House Bill 2502. Capital is section 23-63-1604 and surplus is section 23-63-1605, both amended by Act 554 of 2025. Reporting is section 23-63-1607. Examinations are section 23-63-1608, with the pure-captive cycle added by Act 554. Premium tax is section 23-63-1614, as restated by Act 554. Dormant captives are section 23-63-1624, added by Act 370 of 2017. Act 554 amended only the renewal-fee cross-reference in that section and left the $25,000 capital-and-surplus floor in place. Reporting on generally accepted accounting principles, unless the commissioner approves statutory accounting principles, is section 23-63-1607(b) as amended by Act 521 of 2019. The general examination cycle of at least once every five years is section 23-63-1608(a) as amended by Act 469 of 2023. Act 554 added the seven-year cycle for a pure captive. Application, licence, and renewal fees are 23 CAR section 29-117. The captive rule was effective 12 February 2002 and is now codified as 23 CAR Part 29. Act 554 became Act 554 on 14 April 2025. Bulletin 9-2025 states that 2025 acts without an emergency clause or another stated date took effect on 5 August 2025. Act 554 contains no emergency clause.

min_capital.Pure captive: Unimpaired paid-in capital of not less than $100,000 (section 23-63-1604(a)(1)(B)) and unimpaired surplus of not less than $100,000 (section 23-63-1605(a)(1)(B), reduced from $150,000 by Act 554). The Department's capital table publishes both floors at $100,000.
min_capital.Association captive: An association captive incorporated as a stock insurer maintains unimpaired paid-in capital of not less than $250,000 (section 23-63-1604(a)(1)(C), reduced from $400,000 by Act 554) and unimpaired surplus of not less than $250,000 (section 23-63-1605(a)(1)(C), reduced from $350,000). An association captive incorporated as a mutual insurer maintains unimpaired surplus of not less than $500,000 (section 23-63-1605(a)(1)(E), reduced from $750,000). Section 23-63-1604(a)(1) does not state a separate paid-in capital floor for a mutual association captive. The Department's table lists association capital at $250,000 and association surplus at $250,000 for a stock insurer and $500,000 for a mutual insurer. Act 554 removed the requirement that an association have been in continuous existence for at least one year.
min_capital.Industrial insured captive: An industrial insured captive incorporated as a stock insurer maintains unimpaired paid-in capital of not less than $250,000 (section 23-63-1604(a)(1)(D), raised from $200,000 by Act 554) and unimpaired surplus of not less than $250,000 (section 23-63-1605(a)(1)(D), reduced from $300,000). An industrial insured captive incorporated as a mutual insurer maintains unimpaired surplus of not less than $500,000 (section 23-63-1605(a)(1)(F)). Section 23-63-1604(a)(1) does not state a separate paid-in capital floor for a mutual industrial insured captive. The Department's table lists industrial insured capital at $250,000 and surplus at $250,000 for a stock insurer and $500,000 for a mutual insurer. The Department describes this captive as insuring the risks of the industrial insureds of an industrial insured group or of a risk retention group.
min_capital.Sponsored captive: Unimpaired paid-in capital of not less than $100,000 and unimpaired surplus of not less than $100,000 (sections 23-63-1604(a)(1)(E) and 23-63-1605(a)(1)(G), each reduced from $250,000 by Act 554). The Department publishes both floors at $100,000. The statute and the Department do not state a separate dollar floor for an individual protected cell.
min_capital.Producer reinsurance captive: Unimpaired paid-in capital of not less than $300,000 and unimpaired surplus of not less than $300,000 (sections 23-63-1604(a)(1)(A) and 23-63-1605(a)(1)(A)). Act 554 did not change these amounts. The Department describes this captive as wholly owned by a resident licensed insurance producer, acting only as a reinsurer for risks written by or placed through its parent or an affiliate, and permitted to establish protected cells.
min_capital.Special purpose captive: Capital and surplus are each an amount determined by the commissioner after considering the business plan, feasibility study, and pro formas, including the nature of the risks, but not less than $125,000 (sections 23-63-1604(a)(1)(F) and 23-63-1605(a)(1)(H), each reduced from $300,000 by Act 554). The Department's table publishes $125,000 for both.
min_capital.Branch captive: The Department describes a branch captive as licensed to transact insurance through a business unit with a principal place of business in Arkansas and as operating as a pure captive with respect to those operations. Section 23-63-1604(c) requires a trust fund in the United States, funded by an irrevocable letter of credit or another acceptable asset, for the benefit of United States policyholders and United States ceding insurers. The security may be no less than the capital and surplus required by the subchapter plus the reserves on the branch policies and contracts, including loss reserves, allocated loss-adjustment expenses, incurred-but-not-reported losses, and unearned premiums. The Department's capital table does not state a separate branch dollar floor.
min_capital.Dormant captive: A dormant captive that has been issued a certificate of dormancy possesses and maintains unimpaired paid-in capital and surplus of not less than $25,000 (section 23-63-1624(c)(1)). The section applies to a pure, sponsored, or industrial insured captive that has ceased transacting insurance and has no remaining insurance liabilities. The Department's capital table does not restate this amount.
min_capital.Form and additional capital: Capital may be cash, other assets acceptable to the commissioner, or an irrevocable letter of credit issued by an Arkansas-chartered bank or a Federal Reserve member bank and approved by the commissioner (section 23-63-1604(a)(2)). The commissioner may prescribe additional capital based on the type, volume, and nature of the business (section 23-63-1604(b)). Capital stock of a captive incorporated as a stock insurer is issued at not less than par value.

tax_notes: Section 23-63-1614, as restated by Act 554 of 2025, requires the tax by 1 March. Direct premiums, after return premiums and dividends on unabsorbed premiums or premium deposits returned or credited to policyholders, are taxed at 0.250 percent on the first $20 million, 0.150 percent on the next $20 million, and 0.050 percent thereafter. Assumed-reinsurance premiums are taxed at 0.225 percent on the first $20 million, 0.150 percent on the next $20 million, 0.050 percent on the next $20 million, and 0.025 percent thereafter. Reinsurance tax does not apply to risks taxed on a direct basis, or to a qualifying assumption of loss reserves and other liabilities of another insurer under common ownership and control that is part of a plan to discontinue that insurer and to renew or maintain the business with the captive. If the calculated tax is under $5,000, the tax is $5,000. The total tax may not exceed $100,000 in any year. The Department's premium-tax page states the same rates, minimum, and maximum. A captive may apply the noncommissioned salaries and wages of its Arkansas employees, paid in connection with captive operations, as a credit against the tax. The employee must be employed for six months, have a primary residence in Arkansas, and pay Arkansas income tax. The credit may not reduce the tax by more than 50 percent. Two or more captives under common ownership and control are taxed as one captive. For stock corporations that means direct or indirect ownership of 80 percent or more of the outstanding voting stock. For mutual corporations it means direct or indirect ownership of 80 percent or more of the surplus and the voting power. Branch tax applies only to branch business. The tax is all of the tax collectible under Arkansas law from a captive. No other tax may be levied by the state or a county, city, or municipality, except ad valorem taxes on real and personal property used in the production of income. A producer reinsurance captive that invests and continuously maintains at least 50 percent of its assets in qualifying Arkansas bank certificates of deposit, or in qualifying obligations of the state or of an Arkansas county, city, school district, taxing district, or local improvement district, is not subject to this section. A dormant captive is not liable for the tax. A foreign or alien insurer that redomesticates is liable only for tax on premiums paid after redomestication. It may elect to forgo payment in either its first or its second year of operations, but not both. If it then surrenders its licence or redomesticates away within five years, it immediately pays the forgone tax plus 10 percent a year from the original due date. A redomesticating insurer licensed after 1 July is subject to only one-half of the minimum tax in its first year. The Department requires premium tax and fees to be filed and paid through OPTins.
contact_name: Finance Division, Arkansas Insurance Department
types_allowed: Association captive insurance companies, incorporated as stock or mutual insurers
Sponsored captive insurance companies and protected cells
Producer reinsurance captive insurance companies and protected cells
Dormant pure, sponsored, or industrial insured captives holding a certificate of dormancy
Risk retention groups formed under the Risk Retention and Purchasing Groups Act and made subject to Subchapter 16

fees.licensing_incorporation: 23 CAR section 29-117 requires $200 for filing and review of each application, $300 for the licence when issued, $300 for annual renewal, and an actuarial review fee equal to the cost to the Department. The Department's application instructions state the same non-refundable $200 filing fee, payable to the Arkansas Insurance Department Trust Fund, and state that a $300 fee for the original certificate of authority is requested if the application is approved. Secretary of State organization fees are not set in Part 29 or Subchapter 16.
fees.annual_fees: Annual licence renewal of $300 under 23 CAR section 29-117. A dormant captive pays the licence renewal fee provided in that section. Its certificate of dormancy is renewed every five years. Premium tax and fees are filed and paid through OPTins. The Department's captive pages do not publish a separate dormancy-fee amount.
fees.premium_tax_rate: Direct premiums: 0.250 percent on the first $20 million, 0.150 percent on the next $20 million, and 0.050 percent thereafter. Assumed reinsurance: 0.225 percent, 0.150 percent, 0.050 percent, and 0.025 percent on successive $20 million bands. Annual minimum $5,000. Annual maximum $100,000. Due 1 March. A wage credit for qualifying Arkansas employees may offset up to 50 percent of the tax. A qualifying producer reinsurance captive is outside the section. A dormant captive is not liable for the tax. The tax is in lieu of other state and local taxes except ad valorem taxes on real and personal property used to produce income.

annual_filing_requirements: Before 1 March of each year, or within an extension the commissioner grants for good cause, a captive submits a report of its financial condition verified by the oath of two executive officers. Act 521 of 2019 states that, except as sections 23-63-1604 and 23-63-1605 provide, a captive reports using generally accepted accounting principles unless the commissioner approves statutory accounting principles, with any modifications the commissioner requires. An association captive and an industrial insured group file in the form required by section 23-63-216(a). The Department's filing table assigns quarterly and annual statements to association captives and industrial insured groups, and annual statements only to industrial insured, pure, sponsored, and producer reinsurance captives. A producer reinsurance captive or a pure captive may apply to report on a fiscal year consistent with its parent. The Department states that the report is then due 60 days after fiscal year-end. To support the premium-tax return, the Department's premium-tax page instructs a pure captive to file, before 1 March, pages 1, 2, 3, and 8 of the Captive Annual Statement: Pure or Industrial Insured, verified by two executive officers. 23 CAR section 29-103 requires an annual audit by an independent certified public accountant authorized by the commissioner, filed by 30 June for the preceding calendar year, on the same accounting basis as the annual statement. The audit includes an opinion on the adequacy of loss and loss-expense reserves by a person the commissioner approves who is a Fellow of the Casualty Actuarial Society or a member in good standing of the American Academy of Actuaries. Act 554 allows the commissioner to waive the audit or actuarial opinion for a pure captive whose parent has a consolidated audit, a guaranty of the pure captive's liabilities, minimum net equity of $100 million, and a financial-strength rating of BBB or better from a rating agency the commissioner accepts. A dormant captive files a verified financial-condition report before 15 March. The captive holds at least one board meeting, or a reciprocal's subscribers' advisory committee meeting, each year in Arkansas. It maintains its registered office in Arkansas, or the branch office for a branch captive, and appoints a resident registered agent. At least one director of a corporate captive, and at least one member of a reciprocal's subscribers' advisory committee, is a resident of the United States or a United States territory. Act 469 of 2023 requires an examination at least once every five years, or whenever the commissioner determines it to be prudent, at the company's expense. Act 554 provides that a pure captive is examined at least once every seven years or whenever the commissioner determines it to be prudent. A branch examination is limited to branch business and branch operations if the branch annually provides a certificate of compliance from the jurisdiction where it is formed and demonstrates that it is operating in sound financial condition under that jurisdiction's law. A captive may not provide personal motor vehicle or homeowners insurance or any component of those coverages. It may not accept or cede reinsurance except as authorized by section 23-63-1611. It is not permitted to join or contribute to a state guaranty or insolvency fund or to receive benefits from one. The Department states that pure captives and industrial insured captives are not subject to any restrictions on allowable investments contained in the Arkansas Insurance Code. Act 521 of 2019 requires a sponsored captive to comply with the investment requirements in section 23-63-801, except to the extent credit for reinsurance is allowed under section 23-63-1611 or the commissioner finds another extent reasonable. The same act allows the assets of two or more protected cells to be combined for investment without defeating segregation for accounting or other purposes. It also states that a risk retention group formed under the Risk Retention and Purchasing Groups Act and subject to Subchapter 16 is subject to additional specified provisions of the Insurance Code. The Department's type list does not publish a separate capital floor for that risk retention group.

captive_administrator.name: Finance Division, Arkansas Insurance Department

licensing_speed: Act 554 of 2025 allows the commissioner to issue a provisional licence when the commissioner finds that doing so is in the public interest, after a complete application, payment of all licence fees, and a preliminary finding that the expertise, experience, and character of the persons who will control and manage the applicant are acceptable. The commissioner may limit or revoke the provisional licence. It terminates automatically if the applicant does not complete the regular licensure process. The Act does not state a maximum number of days. The Department describes the ordinary process as quick and efficient and does not publish a standard turnaround.
